column2: It's twelve thirty-five, and that means it's time to put the stuffing bread in oven two at three hundred degrees! Three sheet pans. And fire up the stovetop, because the mushrooms are next!
It's twelve fifty-five! Give that stuffing bread a stir!
It's ten past one! Check the stuffing bread. If it's hard all the way through, pull it out to cool, and crank oven two up to four hundred for the bacon!

Ayy, kick back and listen up. It's one twenty, and you know what time it is. Bacon time, baby. If oven one is hot at four hundred, bacon goes in, eighteen to twenty-five minutes. And don't you dare throw out that fat. That's liquid gold, cuz.
Yo, check that stuffing bread in oven two, nephew. If it's hard all the way through, pull it out to cool and turn oven two off.
It's one thirty, and it's prep time! Trim and halve the Brussels sprouts. Then dice the onion and celery and mince the garlic for the stuffing!
Hold up, hold up. It's one forty. Take a little peek at that bacon in oven one. Is it crispy yet, nephew?
Ten to two, nephew. Take a peek at that bacon in oven one. See if it's getting crispy.
Heads up, friends! In five minutes, we light the Keg!
Ooh wee, almost two! Bacon out of oven one, onto the paper towels. Pour off that bacon fat and save it. Then oven one can kick back until the ham at three fifteen.
It's two o'clock, and it's time to light the Keg! Deflector in, drip pan under the grate, aiming for three twenty-five to three fifty. And get that turkey out of the fridge!
It's two fifteen! Back to the prep station. Peel and seed the butternut squash, and cube all the squash into one-inch cubes. Then whisk up that miso maple glaze!
It's two thirty! Chop the bacon, slice the garlic, chop the rosemary, parsley, mint, chives and scallions, and toast the sesame seeds. Sprouts back in the fridge!
It's two forty-five! Check the Keg. Is it holding steady between three twenty-five and three fifty?
Heads up, friends! The turkey goes on the Keg in five minutes!
It's three o'clock, and the bird is going on! Turkey on the Keg, skin side up, and slide that probe into the thickest part of the breast. Not touching bone!
It's three ten, and it's stuffing mushroom time! Brown them in three batches, eight to ten minutes each. No crowding the pan! Dice the apples for the stuffing while they sizzle.
Quarter past three, nephew, and the ham is going in! Oven one, three twenty-five, covered with foil, in a pan with a splash of water. About ninety minutes.

It's three forty-five! Stuffing mushrooms into a bowl with the tamari. Then butter in the skillet, onion and celery in, then the garlic and spices, then the apples. All of this is the stuffing base, nephew.
It's four o'clock! Quick look at the Keg. Still cruising between three twenty-five and three fifty?
It's four thirty, cuz! Ham comes out, foil off. Stud it with cloves, brush on that glaze, and bump oven one up to three seventy-five.
Hey, friends, quick one. Scalloped potatoes out of the fridge now, so they can come up to room temp before they go in at five thirty.
Easy does it, friends. Fifteen minute warning. Turn the toaster oven downstairs on to three seventy-five now, so it's hot for the brie at five twelve.
It's five o'clock! Preheat oven one to three seventy-five. That's for the potatoes going in at five thirty.

Heads up, cheese lovers. Brie goes in the toaster oven downstairs in five minutes. Somebody grab that wheel, set it in a small baking dish or on a parchment-lined pan, and drizzle that honey all over the top. Get the gluten-free crackers out too, nephew.
Ayy, cheese time, baby. It's five twelve. Brie into the toaster oven downstairs at three seventy-five, fifteen minutes. Let it get nice and melty.
Fifteen minute warning for the potatoes, cuz. Check that oven one actually reads three seventy-five. If it's not there yet, give it a little time. Potatoes go in at five thirty.
Hey, friends, cranberry sauce check! Berries should be popped and saucy. Turn off the heat, scrape it into a bowl, let it cool on the counter, then into the fridge. It thickens as it cools.
It's five twenty, salad crew! Time to get the Caesar lettuce ready. Cut the romaine hearts into inch pieces, wash and dry them completely, then into the fridge, covered.
Heads up, friends! The potatoes go in in five minutes!

Ooh, it's ready. It's five twenty-seven. Brie out of the toaster oven. Let it chill for a couple minutes, hit it with a little more honey, and bring it out with the crackers. Appetizers are served, y'all.
It's five thirty, and the potatoes are going in! Upstairs oven, covered with foil, at three seventy-five. And keep an eye on that turkey, we pull it at one fifty-five in the breast!
It's five forty! Toss the squash cubes with olive oil, salt and pepper, and spread them out on the sheet pans in a single layer, ready to roast.
It's five forty-five, and it's stuffing assembly time! Bread, mushrooms, cranberries, eggs whisked into the broth. Into the nine by thirteen and the eight by eight, dot with butter, cover with foil!
Hey, friends, ham check! Probe the center. When it hits one forty, pull it, tent it with foil, and let it rest. If it is not there yet, give it another ten minutes.

It's six o'clock! Squash cubes go into the upstairs oven with the potatoes, same three seventy-five, on whatever racks are free. They take forty-five to fifty minutes. Mix the focaccia dough, press it into the oiled pan, and let it rise somewhere warm. And how's that ham doing? Pull it at one forty in the center.

It's six oh five, salad crew. Dressing base time, but no mayo yet. In the big wooden bowl, olive oil, garlic, a whole bunch of pepper, lemon juice, Dijon, and the gluten-free Worcestershire. Whisk it, and leave it at the bottom of the bowl. And grate the Parmesan now, about a cup and a half.
Heads up, friends! The stuffing goes in in five minutes!
It's six fifteen, and the stuffing is going in! Oven one, lower rack, covered. Turkey check! Pull it at one fifty-five in the breast!
It's six twenty! Stir the squash cubes and swap the pans, top to bottom.
Focaccia check, friends! It's been about eighteen minutes. If it's golden on top, take it out and let it cool on a rack. It's the appetizer with the clams, so no rush after that.
It's six twenty-five! Toss the squash cubes with half the glaze and back in. Watch it, it can scorch!

It's six thirty! Toss the Brussels sprouts, two pounds plain with olive oil, four pounds with bacon fat, hold the garlic. The oven batch goes into the downstairs oven with the stuffing, three seventy-five, by six thirty-five. And friends, the turkey must come off by six forty!
It's six thirty-five! Uncover the potatoes upstairs. Feeling spicy? A little dusting of togarashi! Sprouts for the oven should be going in the downstairs oven now.
It's six forty! Turkey should be off the Keg by now. Stir the Brussels sprouts on the Keg and add the garlic.
Quick squash check, friends. If a knife slides in easy and the edges are browned, squash out of the oven and cover it loosely with foil. If not, give it five more minutes.
Heads up, friends! Set out the garnishes. Sesame seeds and scallions for the squash. Needed by seven twenty, so anytime before then.
It's six fifty! Uncover the stuffing!
It's six fifty-five! Stir the sprouts in the downstairs oven and add the garlic. Carving in five minutes!
It's six fifty-eight! Check the Keg sprouts. Charred and tender? Then shut the vents down to hold them warm with the lid on. They come off at seven fifteen with everything else. Carving at seven!
It's seven o'clock, and it's carving time! Carve that turkey!
It's seven oh five! Sprouts out of the downstairs oven. Keep them warm, covered, until the table.
Heads up, friends! Potatoes and stuffing come out in five minutes!

It's seven fifteen, and it's the big pull! Potatoes out of the upstairs oven and stuffing out of the downstairs oven. Squash back into an oven for five minutes to rewarm. Keg sprouts off, toss with the parsley and mint, and bacon into the bacon batches!
It's seven sixteen, Caesar crew. Whisk six tablespoons of mayo into that dressing until it's creamy. Lettuce stays in the fridge for six more minutes.
It's seven twenty! Squash out, garnish with sesame, scallions and togarashi. Chives on the potatoes!
It's seven twenty-two, and it's Caesar time! Lettuce into the bowl, toss it good, then Parmesan on top and toss again. Then it goes to the table, nephew.
It's seven twenty-five! Everything to the table! Gobble gobble, you magnificent cooks!
